utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you didn't tell us about this appointment when you were testifying in direct-examination in response to questions by Mr. Nobilo, did you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My testimony did not contain details on every report I issued. Here we can see that until the 4th of September almost 70 documents were issued with the reference number 01. Had I testified on every order, it might have taken two years for me to testify. So I did not have occasion to say anything in this regard because it would have taken up much more time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, after Zuti was shot, you issued documentation to ensure that Zuti, who was shot in a gunfight with another gang, would receive a pension from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, let me repeat before this Tribunal, Zuti was not wounded in this settling of accounts with the gang but in the conflict with the commander named Tuka. Second, for every wounded individual, regardless of the unit he belonged to, I cared for, and that is what I asked my subordinates to do. So for every wounded person to receive a pension and not only a pension but medical treatment and everything necessary under such conditions. I don't know how these pension systems worked and what the legal procedure was. That was done by a separate service within the HVO, a separate department, but I do believe that he received a pension as well because in the first period, he was a member of the military police. When he stopped working for the military police, he was a member of the HVO, just as any other military recruit in the enclave and in the encirclement was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next document on that score, General, another order signed by you on the 24th of October 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 686, 686A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is an order of the 24th of October, 1993. At 1600 -- actually, it is a certificate signed by you delineating Zarko Andric, also known as Zuti, a period of service in the HVO. We will read it: "Certificate. Mr. Zarko Andric, son of Vinko, born 12 June, 1961 in Travnik, has held the following posts in the HVO units: "1. 1 September, 1992, he held the post of commander of the 2nd Company of the 4th Military Police Battalion. He was relieved of this post on 15 March by the head military police administration. "2. April 1993 until 4 July, 1993, he held the post of commander of the special purpose unit of the Frankopan Brigade. "3. Pursuant to Article 34, paragraph 2 of the Decree of the Armed Forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, final version, and the approval of a supreme commander of the armed forces for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna ..." It gives the number of: "... 396/92, dated 27 June, 1992 ..." There's an illegible. "... Mr. Zarko Andric was appointed commander of the Vitez military district for the active duty forces of the Vitez military district (document no. 01-7-71/93)." The previous order. "He will hold this post until further notice." Now, General, this was a document that was executed by you two days after Zuti was shot and paralysed by Tuka and his men; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The document was compiled by my assistant for personnel affairs, Mr. Zoran Pilicic, and I signed the document. It can be clearly seen from the document that he was commander of the military police company, then a member of the Frankopan Brigade and, finally, assistant for the active duty forces. The active forces is something that we were to undertake to form in the future.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from April 1993, when he took a position in the Frankopan Brigade, until the date of this certificate, the 24th of October, 1993, Zuti was under your command as a member of the Frankopan Brigade and then as a member of your staff; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zuti was under the command -- my direct command, and from point 3 you can see that was so from the 7th, 1993. From April 1993, as commander of the special purposes unit of the B formation, he was not under the direct command of the Operative Zone but he was under the direct command of the chief of the main staff or the defence department, depending on how the special purpose unit was registered, although I'm not sure whether that particular special purpose unit ever completed its registration process and the signing of an agreement and whether it was introduced into the structure of the HVO by registration, because there were a lot of changes. If a professional agreement was not signed with the defence department, then he was under the command of the Frankopan Brigade and my own command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You've answered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, are you saying that when he was in the special purpose unit of the Frankopan Brigade, you had no authority to discipline members of the special purpose units of the Frankopan Brigade? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I wasn't able to follow it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Zuti special purpose unit that were part of the Frankopan Brigade, did you or did you not have authority to discipline members of the special purpose unit Zuti which was part of the Frankopan Brigade? Did you or did you not have such authority?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If that special unit was of the B type and registered with the defence department, then I did not have the authority. Neither did the commander of the brigade. If I was not -- I'm not certain whether it had defined its statistic with us and the defence department. So if he did not sign the agreement and contract with the defence department, then that unit was in the formation of the Frankopan Brigade and then I did have disciplinary authority over it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you Defence Exhibits 237 and 239. Take a look at both of them, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is D239; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And 237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We don't have the 237, D237. We don't have it. So try to explain this to us, since you're making comparisons, explain what you're doing, to us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These are two disciplinary orders, that were signed by the accused, of two individuals that were in the PPN Zuti unit as part of the Frankopan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, these two Defence documents reflect that you had the authority to discipline members of the Zuti PPN unit, the special purpose unit, which was part of the Frankopan Brigade and you did, in these two Defence exhibits, 237 and 239; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No translation)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. We're not getting a translation. If you can just hold on. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The date is the 26th of November, 1993, and I just have to look it up in my notes, please. I would like to look at my chronology just to find one date, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, have you found what you're looking for? I think -- do you really need your chronology immediately? I think this is a simple question. On the 26th of November, 1993, did you take disciplinary measures? Is that what you're asking, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, there was a reorganisation of the HVO, and on the 23rd of July or the beginning of August 1993, I had direct command over the military police. Then the special purpose units of the B type were dismantled, that is to say, Tvrtko and all the other B-type units. I do believe that in November that no PPN special purpose unit Zuti existed. So that kind of unit did not exist at all by that time because reorganisation had come into being. Now, I would like to see when that reorganisation actually started. That's why I need to look it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, if you want to look at that during the break, we'll move on to a different question and we'll hold that question in abeyance. We'll just talk about the period of time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, you could do that during the break because these orders have to do with special units. Mr. Boro Lovrenovic, who was sent to the special unit, and Biljaka, who was sent to a special unit. All right. You'll check on that. Please continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, as of the 4th of July, 1993, when you appointed Zuti as an assistant commander of the military district for active duty forces, you certainly had the power to discipline him at that point, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Power over whom? To discipline who?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A member of your staff, Zarko Andric. Zuti. You, as the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, had the power, after you appointed him as a commander, to discipline him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 4th of July, 1993, Zuti did not stop being a thief, did he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have any information of that kind. That he continued to be a thief, I already said that, in fact, he was a merchant and that that's what he -- he traded. So apart from the incident with the military police, there were those who would use his name, but to discover the perpetrator and arrive at him, that was pretty tough, a difficult thing to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, on page 19788, you described Zuti as a local criminal gang leader. Now, after the 4th of July, 1993, did he stop being a local criminal gang leader?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those were rumours that were present in the region, circulating in the region. He never ceased being a leader. But at all events, at that time that was the only way of placing him under control of some kind. I think it was worse to let him do what he wanted, according to his own free will and have him outside any kind of control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, how big was the convoy that Zuti and his men stole on the 15th of April, 1993? How many trucks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were -- I think that was -- the incident with the convoy took place before that, because we tried to return it on the 15th of April, but there were about 30 to 35 motor vehicles in all. There was some passenger cars. I'd have to have a look at my data to see exactly how much. Then we looked at the position where the convoy disappeared from, Putici to Nova Bila. Once again, we had to contact the local leaders. This was in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zuti did it, didn't he? He stole the convoy, he and his men.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Direct information as to the perpetrators, that is to say, who hijacked the convoys, linked to the complete investigation, I never received this information to determine the actual perpetrator, but his men were suspects, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the same guy who breaks people out of gaol, steals convoys, loots - on the 15th it's brought to your attention - that you make the commander on the 4th of July, 1993, it's all the same man, in your efforts to suppress crime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. But you must bear in mind the context in which all this took place. When he attacked the military police, he was a member of the military police. Later on, the military police wouldn't have anything to do with him and left him to work on his own bat, at his own initiative. That was the only way that we could place him under some kind of control, to appoint him commander of an army that did not exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we're going round and round. We're repeating things here. I think the witness has already said all of that. He says that Zuti was appointed by Colonel Blaskic, and then each of you can argue what should be concluded from this or should be deduced from this. Remember your time is at issue here, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, let us move ahead to the period of time when you ran your anti-crime programme Operation Pauk or Operation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kehoe. Let me take advantage of this moment to remind you that there are essential points which are being discussed here. The Judges realise that you still have this week and next week; is that correct? We're going to take a break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. That's what's left approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You, of course, are going to speak to us about Ahmici in the next two weeks, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're going to get there rapidly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You organise your work as you see fit, and, of course, far be it for me to tell you what to do, but we do have some powers according to the Rules. All right. We're going to take a 10-minute or 15-minute break. We're going to suspend the hearing for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume the hearing now. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, let us turn to Operation Pauk. Was Zuti arrested during Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no, but it's very difficult for me to answer because there were over 360 persons who were arrested during the Operation Pauk, during a very short period of time, but I think he was not arrested because the executive part of the Operation Pauk, I'm not sure whether it was carried out in that area. But I believe that during the preparatory stage, they did look at him, but there was a problem of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us give the witness Defence Exhibits 267, 268, and 269, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is this Defence or Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These, of course, are your orders of the 15th of April and the early morning hours of the 16th of April. Now, General, before we get into those orders, I want to read some of your testimony beginning on page, I believe it is, 18490. If there's a pagination problem, counsel, it may be 18479. It begins on line 12, questioned by Mr. Nobilo: "Q After that --" And we are talking about the 15th of April. "Q After that, you had another meeting dealing with the abduction of that big convoy, the 15 trucks and 30 passenger vehicles with humanitarian aid. What were the conclusions of that meeting? A I had a meeting with the assistant for security because I was interested whether anything had been done following that request for return of goods, and the conclusion was that the military police were not able to retrieve this equipment, even though we knew at the time that the vehicles were parked on the side of the road between Han Bila and Nova Bila. Q Why was the military police not able to retrieve those vehicles? A One of the answers was that an armed group was much more powerful than the police forces available and that an order for the military police to be able to carry out this, it would have to use force, and the armed group that was holding the convoy was much stronger." Before we continue on with the reading, General, this armed group that was much stronger than the military police was Zuti and his men; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The armed group that held up the convoy mostly consisted of members of the criminal groups from the municipalities of Travnik, Novi Travnik, and partly the municipality of Vitez too. Some of them said that they were members of Zuti but not all of them were from that part of the Travnik municipality, that is to say, there were groups from Novi Travnik and from Vitez. It was hard to identify who stood behind this, but these were very strong and very mobile armed groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me continue reading on at 18480, line 6, the continuation of your testimony: "A ... The chief of staff, Mr. Nakic, happens to live very near Nova Bila, and he called me on the telephone and confirmed that the vehicles from this convoy were still in Nova Bila, but he told me, 'I'm afraid those forces would mean nothing to these criminal groups.' Q So what did you decide to do in order to solve this problem? A The assistant for security suggested that we invite members of the military police, that is, the commander of the military police to a meeting and also to invite the commander of the Vitezovi, a representative of this group, his name was Zuti, and a member of the Tvrtkovci unit and to present to them the overall situation and problems that had arisen in connection with the taking of these goods and to ask for their assistance in retrieving them. Q Was this meeting organised and did they show up? A This meeting took place somewhere around 17.00 and they did show up at it." So you have described the individual who was a representative of this group who stole the convoy as Zuti, did you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was an individual who was present or, rather, invited to attend the meeting on the basis of the proposal of the assistant for security, together with the others who were present at the meeting. We certainly believed that he was the one who could help in returning the convoy because, unfortunately, the armed force of the military police was out of the question there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on page 18485, we begin the discussion of the reading of Defence Exhibit 267 and 268, the preparatory combat order which is 267 and the order to take action which is 268. You say at line 19, "I took both these orders and I read them out orally to the commanders present at the meeting." Now, the commanders who were present at the meeting to whom you read those orders were Pasko Ljubicic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zarko Andric, Zuti?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about line 18 of your testimony, you note that Zuti was present.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I note that a member of Tvrtko was present. Let me just find this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, would you like me to read your pertinent testimony regarding Zuti again, as being present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he was present at the meeting, but I'm not sure whether he was present when I was reading the order, during that part of the meeting, but I know that he was invited to the meeting and that he was present at the meeting. Could you please read that part of my testimony to me just to remind me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You note: "I took both these orders and I read them out orally to the commanders present at the meeting. After I had read out the provisions of the order, after I had read them out, we concluded the meeting."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My pagination may be a tad off here, counsel, but I think it's 18485 at 19 or 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is. Where is the reference to Zuti? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The reference to Zuti, I believe, is at 18480, and his specific reference is line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What are you looking for, General Blaskic? What is the purpose of your search? You have just been read your statement.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm trying to find in the transcript my own testimony in order to remind me of this, and I'm trying to find this meeting and the circumstances. I know who was invited to the meeting, but a different part of the meeting was read out to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For the time being, you've simply been asked whether Zuti was at the meeting. Isn't that right, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Prosecutor explicitly told me that in my testimony, I highlighted that Zuti was present at the meeting too when I read the order out, and now I tried to find it in my own testimony, that part of my statement, because I know that the order related to the members of the military police, Vitezovi, and Tvrtko, the commander of Tvrtko in that part in which I read the orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you can find it at another date. We'll eliminate Zuti from the equation at this point, and we'll ask the questions about the other special purpose units and the military police in reference to Exhibits 267 and 268. You noted for us in Exhibit 267 and 268 that there are actual activities to be taken in the field by the 4th Military Police Battalion in Exhibit 267 and the Vitezovi, also in 267, and yet further activity to be taken by the anti-terrorist platoon of the military police in Exhibit 268. General, my question concerns those units. At the time you issued those orders, you knew that there were criminals in the military police and you knew that there were criminals in the Vitezovi - we won't go into Zuti at this point - but for those two particular units, you knew that there were criminals. In those orders, did you order any special precautions to ensure that those criminals in those two units did not engage in any activities pursuant to these orders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, we have to make certain distinctions in terms of criminals until these orders, and according to the information I received, not a single one of these persons committed a war crime. According to the information I had, it was not committed. Secondly, I did particularly bear in mind that all protagonists of criminal activity should be expelled from these units, and this can be seen from my chronology. I kept sending in requests to that effect. In 268 and in document 267, I very specifically defined this, particularly because of all the problems involved, I defined the objective of this activity and I limited the use of force, especially from the point of view of command and control. I spelled out very precisely in a special section that I had to be informed about all extraordinary events, that is to say, that the orders are very specific and precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you do anything in these orders to ensure that the people that you wanted to eliminate, these criminals that you wanted to eliminate from the military police and the Vitezovi, did not engage in activities that you ordered in 267 and 268? Did you do anything, and if you did, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, you're asking me about these people, the 4th Battalion of the military police. I said that they had people who had a criminal record, and the ATG platoon of the 4th Battalion, I don't know whether it had such persons or not, this was a newly established unit according to the criteria of the military police administration. Furthermore, in order to prevent any kind of arbitrariness on the part of these individuals within the units, I spelled out very precisely in one of the items of this order, I said very specifically and very precisely -- if you read each and every point, you will see that it is very clearly defined, very precisely defined, what should be done, how it should be done, when it should be done, and when I should be informed about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the bottom line is that you took no precautions, did you, to ensure that these criminals were not involved in these operations; isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I acted according to the provisions that were binding on me as commander, and I spelled out all the documents precisely. As for the decision, it can be seen in document 268. The commander of the unit knows his soldiers best of all, and it is up to him to decide who he is going to engage and how. I used all my abilities in order to exercise the greatest possible command control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you include any admonition in any of these orders to these brigades and these units that they have to protect and watch out for civilians? Did you include that anywhere in any of these orders, and if you did, could you point it out to us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The protection of civilians is a legal obligation for all, absolutely all persons, and in orders, we said what the doctrine of writing orders contains. Every order that I wrote was written in accordance with the doctrine that I was trained according to, and you can also look at a document called "Guidelines for Writing Orders," and you can see that it is all spelled out very precisely. This is done in great detail. It should be done this way by a platoon commander or a company commander at the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you testified in response to questions by Mr. Nobilo to two things, that you were dealing with a peasant army and that you had criminals in these units. Under those circumstances, as a commander, do you believe that you had to do more to ensure that the troops would protect civilians or less?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see, this question, what I think and what I thought would perhaps require a longer answer. From the moment I came, I did my best. There were thousands of soldiers going to Jajce, and I tried to tell every one of them about the importance of humane treatment in the battlefield and the humane treatment of all civilians. In September 1992, I issued a special document which specifically establishes the code of conduct for soldiers on the battlefield. However, I did not have any information as to anyone having committed a war crime before the 16th of April, and not a single one of these units committed a war crime according to the information that I had. These orders were written according to the doctrine according to which I was trained, and they are far more precise because of the level of the commanders. Each and every one of these items can be analysed, and you can see that the place of operation, and the point of operations, and the purpose of operations, and the command over this command. Had every one of these commanders acted the way they should have, they would have informed me about each and every one of these events, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you've already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you had information, prior to issuing this order, that in Busovaca, at least where the Vitezovi was involved, that 53 houses had been burnt to the ground and another 112 had been damaged in the HVO-controlled area.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that the problem of the conflict in Busovaca was regulated and resolved through the joint commission in Busovaca and that it was being resolved through the European Monitoring Mission. The total number of houses burnt is three times larger, although this is not really an argument, on the Croatian side as compared to the Bosniak Muslim side. The problem was the identity of the perpetrators. In order to understand this sufficiently, you have to bear in mind the situation prevailing in Busovaca and where the houses were burned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That was not quite the question asked of you, General Blaskic. I think the question was to know whether, in light of why it was done in Vitezovi, specials measures were necessary. I think you've already answered. You said that you had taken certain specific measures. I think we have got to move forward.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Vitezovi does not take part in Busovaca, according to my orders. This can be seen from the 250 documents related to Vitezovi, and I did not give any orders of this nature then and nor did I have any information that the Vitezovi took part in what happened in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, you said with these orders that you gave very specific instructions to your troops. Take a look at 268. In 268, you tell the anti-terrorist platoon, the Jokers, to engage in activities to eliminate these terrorist groups; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry, which item are you reading now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm reading paragraph 2. Paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3 in Exhibit 268.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: 2.3 relates to the military police; 2.2 does not pertain to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your counsel said that you should read this and the other order together. Is that wrong or do we read these paragraphs individually?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Form of the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand which way we should read these. Mr. Nobilo asked the witness whether or not we should read these two orders together and these paragraphs together, and the witness said, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You have to demonstrate what you're trying to show, Mr. Prosecutor. We're a bit lost here. What is the point of your question? You want to show that the witness has given very specific argument, especially in points 2.2 and 2.3; is that right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the specificity of your orders. We have established that you didn't include any special cautions on the protection of civilians. Let's talk about what you told the anti-terrorist platoon, to engage in fighting diversionary terrorist groups of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and we'll focus just on 2.3. You gave specific instructions to them to fight diversionary groups of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: 2.3 is quite clear here. Within --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me try to put things back in order because things are not moving right. I think that the witness answered -- well, you asked him several times whether he had taken any measures insofar as he was in a position to know things about the qualitative composition of delinquents and criminals in the units. You want to know whether he took any precautionary measures. Now we're having a dialogue of deaf people here. The witness says that very specific orders were given, 267, 268. I think the question is to ask Mr. Blaskic whether, in the very specific orders, one finds a trace of measures having to do with a certain degree of prudence in light of the composition of some of the special units like the Vitezovi or the Jokers. The witness also answered that question, Mr. Prosecutor. He said, more or less, that he had applied orders according to military doctrine that he had learned at the academy, I assume, and that as regards the law, it was self-evident. Perhaps the question that could be asked, even if it is self-evident, is: General Blaskic, in 268, for example, is there a trace of any type of prudence that you had demonstrated? That's what I want to be brought out. Then you can argue about that in the final arguments. Otherwise, we're not going to get out of this. Listen to my question, Mr. Blaskic. In the different orders, can we find a trace of any precaution that you would have taken in light of the fact that your units are composed of peasant soldiers, criminals, thugs, people who always wanted to get into fights? That's the question. Look at 268. It seems that that's the document that we were looking at.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I answer that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Not only can you, you can answer it, but you must answer it. All right. We're waiting to hear what you have to say.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, in document 268, in point number 1, everything I knew was spelled out in detail about the forces of the 7th Muslim Brigade, that is to say, a religious unit within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, about its activity, its terrorist activities, about acts that are well-known until then, and their forms of operating. Also, what is mentioned in detail is the deployment of this unit, in the first point. Then it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're still not answering the question, General Blaskic, or else it's going to be very long. Try to be more concise. The question is a simple one. Is there a trace in your order of any measures which show certain precautions in respect of the civilian populations? I understand the answer you want to answer, saying that in light of the terrorist nature among the Muslims, you wanted to counter the terrorism. That's not really what the question is.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I took special measures because in 2.3, when I gave tasks to the 4th Battalion of the military police, I once again said that the task of that unit is to act in the areas where the 7th Muslim Brigade was deployed. You see, it says so in 2.3, that is to say, within areas of operation, location of the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It has a double meaning. We'll move to another question and you can argue that in your closing argument. You're giving a two-edged argument because points 2 and 3 state clearly that you are in the act of establishing some kind of anti-terrorist brigades that were particularly rapid and energetic. Now, when you have a brigade that is to fight terrorism rapidly, one could ask whether they might be a little too energetic and too rapid in their responses.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see -- Mr. President, let me just say one thing. It is unusual that in point 2.3, again I'm referring to point 1, that is outside the doctrine, that is to say, that I'm telling the commander once again, in 2.3, to bear in mind point 1. So this is deviation from the doctrine because I want to underline once again what the point of this operation is. Furthermore, as far as security and safety measures are concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But safety measures for whom? Let me read this for the public: "3. Security and protection measures." The title is attractive, but we have to understand what is being protected, what is being made secure. "Security measures at command posts and commanding officers." The Prosecutor's question was not that. It was to prefer all useless, pointless, movements, to ensure protection of all information. This has to do with protecting civilians, not information that is moving between the superiors and subordinates. I think this is a dialogue which isn't going anywhere, and you can go back to it when you have your final arguments. You say what you say, the Prosecutor says what he says, and the Defence says what it says. I don't think we can go any further than that. We want things to move forward, after all. I don't want to take the floor from you, General Blaskic, but try to move things forward. You speak about protective and security measures in the order, if I understand you correctly, but they're not protective measures for civilians, if I understand the translation correctly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I meant to draw your attention to point 6 where command and control is mentioned, where, for the purposes of command and control, I'm saying that the system of control and command should be in continuity at all levels, that there should be an uninterrupted system of direction, and the command is to be secured at all levels, and that the regular reports are to be sent in, that is to say, in order to exercise the command and control over these units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's your answer. We note it as having been given that way, and we have no further comments to make about it. Mr. Kehoe, move on to another question in this subject or another subject or have I completely demolished your cross-examination? Excuse me if I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's quite all right, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm just trying to move things forward. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, let's look at order 268 where you give this order to the anti-terrorist platoon of the military police, in 2.3. This is the anti-terrorist platoon of the military police, the Jokers; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this order where you allege that you are being specific, do you anywhere describe what one of this terrorists looks like, how they're dressed? Do you describe that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Which terrorists? I don't know which you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The terrorists from the 7th Muslim Brigade that you're discussing in 2.3.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All the data that I had about the 7th Muslim Brigade is contained in point 1. A description of what they looked like, of what the members of the anti-terrorist group looked like, I don't know. I never saw a military order of that nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I assume that you had reconnaissance platoons out patrolling, trying to find out who these people were, what they looked like, and where they were located specifically, didn't you, before you issued this order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, of course we had information who those individuals were and where they were located. We had that information, and that is what point 1 states. Now, as to what they looked like, those in the field knew what they usually looked like, what those members usually looked like, but I don't know the order of any commander who would say they look like that, they wear such and such a uniform, and their aspect is the following, because the diversionary groups are usually made up of three to five soldiers. They're very speedy in their operations. They are usually masked in some way and are detected too late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell this anti-terrorist group, the Jokeri, that they are free to operate in the municipalities of Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In point 2.3, it is stated that they should act according to the diversionary terrorist groups of the 7th Muslim Brigade where it is located in point 1 of this particular order. So in the first paragraph, I refer to point 1 of order 268, and the bulk of the activity should be in the municipalities of Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez. That unit was intended to counteract diversionary terrorist groups, and the diversionary terrorist groups appear suddenly in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. Let's take that comparison. In paragraph 1, where are the 7th Muslim Brigade troops in Busovaca? Where do you describe them in paragraph 1? They're not there, are they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are not in the Busovaca area, but they are in the first neighbouring municipality. The diversionary terrorist groups never base themselves in the territory in which they are operating. They will go out, perform their operations, and withdraw to their base. So when, in point 1, the deployment of forces is mentioned, it mentions that part of the men are from Kakanj in Zenica, in neighbouring municipalities, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are they in Vitez, according to paragraph 1? Because you tell the Jokeri that they can operate in Vitez as well. Where are they, the 7th Muslim Brigade, listed in paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that the diversionary terrorist groups are manifesting their activities, that is to say, we usually learn about it once they have completed their operations. But parts of the 7th Muslim Brigade units were in Stari Vitez and in the area of Preocica, Poculica. That's where those sections were. They could launch their operations from that area in any of the positions in Vitez municipality, and so could the ones from Zenica, because it wasn't very far off either. In fact, they did come in October 1993. They came from Ravno Rostovo and were operational in Rastovci, in the Novi Travnik municipality. They weren't in the town of Novi Travnik, but they launched their operation in Novi Travnik, in the town proper, and they came from Rastovci with the help of a convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, do you think it was important for the Jokeri to know that you knew that there were no anti-terrorist groups in Ahmici? Do you think that was significant?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know and everybody knows that there were no anti-terrorist groups in Ahmici. According to all the reports that we received, no such groups existed in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question was: Do you think it was significant to inform the Jokeri that there were no anti-terrorist groups in Ahmici? Do you think that was important?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In point 1, it was important to enumerate all the data and information we had as to where the 7th Muslim Brigade was based. Had I enumerated all the villages where there were no anti-terrorist groups, then it would be important to mention all the villages in the Vitez-Busovaca municipalities and, in fact, all the municipalities in Central Bosnia, but I set out in precise detail all the information I had in paragraph 1, that is to say, where the units of the 7th Muslim Brigade were located and everything that we had knowledge of at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, looking at this particular order, the actual choice of when the Jokeri was to operate was up to the commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was also said to the other commanders as well, because we cannot know when a contact would be made and when a diversionary terrorist group would be discovered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by your order, General, the Jokeri was permitted to operate in Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez with no specific instructions as to where the 7th Muslim Brigade was located, and they were allowed to do it at their own time frame; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not right, because in point 2.3, I refer back to paragraph 1 of this order, paragraph 1 stipulates, in great detail, everything that was known about the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, that is to say, everything that they had done up till then, what they intended to do in the future and the concrete deployment of all command elements that we had linked to the 7th Muslim Brigade, so that it was very precisely stated. The basic command of the anti-terrorist groups, from the regulations of military groups, was to fight diversionary terrorist groups because that is why these units existed, for assignments of this kind, and that was their intentions. The term says so, "Anti-terrorist platoon." But I limit it to the municipalities where there had already been terrorist activities of this kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, when you said a moment ago, "Everybody knows that there were no anti-terrorist groups in Ahmici," would you have been including in that the 4th Military Police Battalion and the Jokers?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I did because the Jokers were used from the end of December 1992. They used a facility near the village of Ahmici, and there were never any major incidents. I do believe that had anti-terrorist groups existed, then probably they would have become manifest. However, there could have been the involvement and engagement of anti-terrorist groups from Preocica in the area of the village of Ahmici, which means that they weren't based there, they did not have their base there, but they could have been infiltrated into the region because that is what usually happens. They are infiltrated into the area in which they engage in their operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question. Exhibit D268A was issued by you on 15 April, 1993 at 15.45.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You issued an order of action. What's the English, Mr. Kehoe? I have the French before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is "Order to take action" on 268.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: "Order to take action." Is my impression correct that this order was issued by you both to independent brigades, such as the 4th Military Police Battalion, and also to normal HVO formations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is my impression then correct that in this order, you were issuing instructions on the basis of authority to all of these formations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the basis of the competence I had and the orders which, on the 15th of April, I was given by the chief of the main staff in the case of an all-out general attack by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And this order would remain in force on the following day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this order was to have remained in force. In the case of an attack, then all the units which were not directly subordinated to me were to be attached to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us summarise this particular order. You tell the Jokeri to go and "Take prisoner and destroy by quick and energetic actions diversionary terrorist groups of the 7th [Muslim] brigade ..." You then tell them to "... destroy the accommodation facilities and return to base without accepting fighting." The area that they are to cover are the municipalities of Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez, and the commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion can decide when he wants to do this. General, that is a carte blanche to this unit to go and do what you want to do, go where you want to go, and go and do it when you want to do it; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, the interpretation I had received was that I commanded that prisoners of war be taken prisoner or even to be destroyed. That is not correct and that is not what this order states. Second, I have already said why I mentioned the areas of operation. You see that Busovaca, Zenica, Novi Travnik, and Vitez are mentioned, and they were the only areas in which the unit could be effective, that is to say, units intended to fight diversionary terrorist groups. This task, this assignment was copied out from the regulations of any, if we were to open it, military regulations treating fights against diversionary and terrorist groups. I refer to the rules of company, platoon, battalion, brigades, rules and regulations governing them, the armed forces of the former Yugoslav People's Army, in fact. This was the type of formulation that was used in fighting diversionary terrorist groups. These were the principles to be adhered to, linked to arrests and so on, but I never read that prisoners should be liquidated, and it is not true. In order to ensure command control, I demand that the system of command be allowed to function intact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that's been said already. I didn't hear any question when you were speaking about liquidating prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I don't know what the translation was. I was reading the order, Mr. President, which says: "Take prisoner and destroy by quick and energetic action diversionary terrorist groups of the 7th [Muslim] brigade." That is the first line in the second paragraph at 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. If the interpretation is not good, of course, you cannot answer the question properly, General. But the question remains, and I would like you to try to answer it, we have a few moments left, the question is to know whether you gave carte blanche to those units to carry out quick and energetic actions in the zones within the municipalities of Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez. If you say that that was in accordance with the military doctrine of Yugoslavia, well, I wouldn't know whether that is so, but the question is an important one.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not issue an order, as the Prosecutor maintains, and I refer to point 6 of this order where I demand, in very precise terms, that I be informed of all the details and exceptionally if the need arises. So I demand reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But the reports are done after the action has been carried out. We're talking about taking "quick and energetic actions in order to destroy diversionary terrorist groups of the 7th [Muslim] brigade," to destroy accommodations, and to "return to the base without accepting fighting." The activities are to be undertaken within the municipalities of Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already stated that this is the point that corresponds in content to all the principles and regulations of the former Yugoslav People's Army. When we describe, according to the rules of the former JNA, fighting against diversionary and terrorist groups, then these are the actions that have to be stipulated in the second half of 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, that's an answer. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the reality of this situation is that when the Jokeri went in and massacred those people in Ahmici, you have provided yourself a perfect out by giving a vague order allowing these guys to do anything they wanted to do; isn't that right, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not so. So please give me any rule and regulation for us to see whether the order was written in precise terms, as required by the rules and regulations, when dealing with fighting diversionary groups. I demanded that the system of the chain of command, control and command, be affected and when they entered. Then I learned at this Tribunal from the Prosecution witnesses what happened, but until the 16th of October, until 12.45, I had no direct knowledge as to the events that had taken place in the area. On the basis of this order, I say that they cannot have committed a war crime and that no soldier could have committed a war crime on the basis of this document because the order is very precise, and there is no corps commander who writes an order in as much detail as this order has been written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, they did go in there on the morning of the 16th and massacre those people, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You quite possibly know this. I told you what I knew about what was linked to the perpetrators. Unfortunately, I do not have the identity of the perpetrators to this day. If I did have, I am certain that they would have been prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's after 6.00. I'm about to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. I think you're right. We're going to stop here. We are adjourning until tomorrow at 2.00. The court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
